title: Pulse-width modulation
body: Pulse-width modulation (PWM) means switching a motor's power fully on and off very fast. That's hundreds or thousands of times a second. The duty cycle is the share of the time the power is on.

Those pulses are too quick for the motor to follow. Its coil smooths out the current, and its spinning parts smooth out the speed. Think of quick, regular pushes on a playground roundabout: it keeps turning smoothly. So the motor settles at a steady speed set by the average voltage. Switch slowly enough, though, and it really would jerk.
Average voltage = duty cycle × supply voltage. At 50% duty on 6 V, the motor gets 3 V on average. It spins at roughly half speed.
equation: average voltage = duty cycle × supply voltage
realWorld: Computer fans, drones and dimmable LED lights all use PWM to set their speed or brightness.
sources: Condit, R. AN905 Brushed DC Motor Fundamentals. Microchip Technology, DS00905B. https://ww1.microchip.com/downloads/en/AppNotes/00905B.pdf
